note: Worked examples. These groups are excluded from every queue, group count, member count, time total and accuracy figure.

examples.title: BGL worked example
examples.summary: Template <*> L3 <*> error(s) (dcr <*> detected and corrected — component KERNEL, level INFO.
examples.sample: … RAS KERNEL INFO 1 L3 EDRAM error(s) (dcr 0x0157) detected and corrected
steps: Read the header: component KERNEL, severity INFO. Rule B-N01 is the first BGL rule: the severity is not FATAL or FAILURE.
Open the Fields tab: field 1 is a count, field 2 is EDRAM or directory, field 3 is a register address. No value can turn an INFO line into an alert.
Click a few messages to read their raw lines, and open the context of one line. Every line shows RAS KERNEL INFO.
examples.explanation: B-N01 decides for every line of the group: the severity is INFO. The word “error” in the message does not matter; only FATAL and FAILURE lines can be alerts, and only when an alert rule matches. Label for the group: Normal.

examples.title: Thunderbird worked example
examples.sample: acpid: acpid startup succeeded  /  acpid: acpid shutdown succeeded
steps: Go through T-A01 … T-A10: no alert phrase appears in the template, and field 2 only takes the values startup / shutdown, which cannot complete any alert phrase.
Click each of the two messages to read their raw lines.
Open the context of a line: it sits in a run of service start / stop records written while a node boots or shuts down. Context does not change the label; it only confirms what you read.
examples.explanation: No rule T-A01 … T-A10 applies to any line of the group, so T-N01 decides. Label for the group: Normal.

examples.title: HDFS worked example
examples.summary: Count vector: allocate T22×1; write three replicas T5, T9, T11, T26 ×3 each; read T3×1 and T4 (Got exception while serving) ×2; verify T2×3; file deletion T23, T21 ×3 each.
steps: H-A01: none of the failure events T7, T8, T10, T12, T13, T14, T17, T20, T24, T27, T28, T29, T31, T32 is in the count vector.
H-A02: the write is complete (T22 ≥ 1, T5 ≥ 3, T9 ≥ 3, T11 ≥ 3, T26 ≥ 3). H-A03: there is no T25. H-U01: no T1, T15, T19. H-N02: no T25.
Open the full log of 2–3 blocks and compare two of them: their event orders differ, but every one is write 3 replicas → read and verify → delete 3 replicas. T4 belongs to the read phase.
examples.explanation: No rule above H-N01 applies, so H-N01 decides. All blocks of the group share the count vector, so the group gets one label: Normal. The order of events does not matter.
